key_insight: PPG-LM aligns wearable/monitor-derived PPG signals with EHR context at segment, event, and visit levels to make physiological waveforms more language- and clinically aware.
clinical_relevance: If validated, this could improve how continuous PPG data are summarized, retrieved, and used for downstream clinical prediction across wearables and hospital monitoring.
method: Automatic captioning pipeline creates segment-, event-, and visit-level text from PPG measurements plus structured EHR data.
Two-stage training: contrastive learning and waveform-conditioned captioning establish segment-language alignment first.
Time-aware aggregation and temporal statement matching extend alignment to longer clinical events and visits.
evidence_signal: Pretrained on about 73k hours of PPG and evaluated on MC-MED, MIMIC-III, and VitalDB, with improved retrieval, caption factuality, and gains on multiple clinical prediction tasks.
watch_item: The approach depends on high-quality EHR-linked captions and may face generalization and implementation challenges when clinical records are sparse, noisy, or temporally misaligned with PPG.
paper_title: PPG-LM: A Photoplethysmography-Language Model with Multi-Level Clinical Alignment
